question: An electronics retailer offers two successive discounts of 7% and 10% on a TV priced at ₹48,000. What is the difference in the final price after applying two successive discounts compared to applying a flat discount of 17%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For successive discounts of x% and y%, the difference between a flat (x + y)% discount and the successive discounts is directly given by (x × y) ÷ 100 %.

Given successive discounts: 7% and 10%.

Difference in discount % = (7 × 10) ÷ 100 = 0.7%

Difference in Final Price = 0.7% of ₹48,000

Difference = (0.7 ÷ 100) × 48000 = ₹336

**∴ The correct answer is ₹336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the TV = ₹48,000

First case: Successive discounts of d₁ = 7% and d₂ = 10%

Second case: Flat discount of D = 17%

**Formula Used:**

Effective successive discount % = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100

 
 
 

 
 

 
 ₹48,000

 

 

 
 Flat 17% Discount = ₹8,160

 
 7% & 10% Discount = ₹7,824

 

 
 Diff = ₹336

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective successive discount = 7 + 10 − (7 × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ Effective successive discount = 17 − 0.7 = 16.3%

⇒ Difference between flat discount and successive discount = 17% − 16.3% = 0.7%

⇒ Difference in final price = Difference in actual discount amount

⇒ Difference = 0.7% of ₹48,000

⇒ Difference = (0.7 ÷ 100) × 48000 = 0.7 × 480 = 336

**∴ The correct answer is ₹336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of x% and y% are applied on an item, the overall effective discount is calculated using the formula: Effective Discount = x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100.

Flat vs Successive Discount

For the same numerical sum of percentage discounts, a single flat discount will always be greater than applying them successively. The percentage difference exactly equals the interaction term (x × y) ÷ 100.

Selling Price Formula

The selling price after a discount is evaluated as SP = MP × (100 − D) ÷ 100, where MP is the Marked Price and D is the final effective discount percentage.
